requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.ci.span`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request any implementation source. Each obligation maps to tests and assertions as follows.

**Opening fence**
- The opening fence needs at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. In `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]`, `definition_blocks` returns no block for each of these inputs:
  - `::{req}`, which has too few colons.
  - `::: {req}`, which has a space before `{req}`.
  - `:::{req}ready`, which has no space before the name.
- Four-colon and seven-colon openers are accepted in `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]`.
- A three-space-indented opener is accepted, and a four-space-indented opener is rejected, in `fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]`.

**Closing fence**
- A closer needs at least as many colons as the opener. Longer closers (`::::`/`:::::` and `:::::::`/`::::::::`) are accepted in `fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]`.
- A shorter nested `:::` does not close a `::::` block in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]`. It asserts the exact body range and that the text after the closer is excluded.
- A closer must have nothing else on its line except whitespace. `:::foo` does not close the block, and `::: ` with trailing whitespace does. Both are asserted on exact body ranges in `fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]`.
- A closer indented by three spaces is accepted. A closer indented by four spaces leaves the block unclosed (`!unclosed[0].closed`).
- A missing closer produces a validation error naming the file, line and requirement in `fn[reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence]`.

**Body content**
- The body includes all Markdown between the fences. `fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` uses a body containing a code block, a `:::` line inside that block, an ATX heading and a setext heading, and blank lines. The recorded requirement must equal it, or validation fails.
- The same test shows the following requirement and the "Outside the requirement." text are not absorbed into the first body.
- `fn[validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines]` and `fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]` also cover bodies with `{req}` text in a code block and with nested directives.
- Text after the closing fence is excluded. This is asserted in the nested-directive test and in the longer-closer test, where "Outside the requirement." must not be part of the body.

**Option lines**
- Option lines are excluded from the body. In `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text]`, `without_options` is asserted to remove only the header option lines. Inline `:impl:` and `:test:` text that is not immediately after the opening fence stays in the body.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` asserts there is no "text changed" error when the options are present.

**Whitespace**
- `fn[requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace]` has a body with leading indentation and trailing spaces. It validates cleanly against the trimmed recorded text.

**Ambiguity and non-gaps**
- One point is ambiguous but is not a gap. The text does not say whether a `:::` line inside a Markdown code block closes the requirement. The tests assert that it does not, which fits the text's "including … examples, diagrams". They assert this on a single scenario, and the text never requires the opposite.
- I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the text.

text: :::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
